summary: Recovering closed guard is an option when an opponent shuts down half-guard offense.
description: A short explanation of half-to-closed-guard recovery based on Stephan Kesting’s public article.
overview: Half guard offers sweeps and submissions, but an opponent may shut down those attacks. Stephan Kesting’s article on returning to closed guard presents changing position as a useful response. It describes a butterfly-hook recovery demonstrated by Roberto “Gordo” Correia, making recovery part of the half-guard discussion rather than treating another attack as the only answer.

fits: Your half-guard attacks stall and you want to understand the option of recovering closed guard.

includes: Why a player might leave half guard and recover closed guard when offense is being shut down.
limits: This topic covers one recovery option and its purpose, not a complete half-guard attacking system.

sources.title: How to Transition from Half to Closed Guard — Stephan Kesting

flashcards.question: Is staying in half guard always the goal when its attacks are being shut down?
flashcards.answer: No. Kesting’s article discusses recovering closed guard as another choice, rather than repeatedly forcing the same half-guard game.
